newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES EDGE HIGHER IN LOWER VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES EDGE HIGHER IN LOWER VOLUME.

text.p: A quiet Istanbul market firmed slightly in selective trading on Friday after some disappointment over the results of a Higher Board of Privatisation (OYK) meeting late on Thursday, brokers said.

"Activity died down and trade margins narrowed, but there wasn't any pessimism. The approval of only a few sell-offs at yesterday's privatisation meeting depressed activity," said Berra Kilic from Ata securities.
The IMKB National-100 closed five points, or 0.3 percent firmer at 1,654, bringing weekly gains to 10.34 percent after last week's 3.88 percent rise prompted by fading political tension.
Trade volume shrank to 32.93 trillion lira from 45.48 trillion on Thursday.

The privatisation of three banks, a cement firm, a tyre maker and a maritime cargo company for $600 million were passed by the OYK. A total of 20 sell-off tenders whose negotiations were finalised in December and January were awaiting its approval with a total best bid value of $881.7 million.
Privatisation hopes had enlivened earlier this week ahead of the Board meeting, buoying demand in state-controlled firms.
"Selective activity may continue in light of first quarter profit prospects from now on because the release of all 1996 financial reports (this week) ended expectations," Kilic said.

Of the 238 shares traded, 104 advanced, 76 declined and 58 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial was unchanged at 1,659, the IMKB Services rose 1.03 percent to 1,567 and the IMKB Financial firmed 0.99 percent to 1,733.
Actives were led by leading car maker Tofas, up 900 lira at 9,800 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 232,500. They made 20 percent of the total turnover.
